_notes: Frozen Phase 1B query specification for the Q1 (embedding model) / Q2 (retrieval query construction) experiment. target_disease is declared independently of query_text per methodological review -- evaluation must look up target_disease directly, never infer it by parsing query_text. query_type 'vlm_caption' has query_text=null; it is filled in at execution time from a real Qwen3-VL caption of a real PlantVillage image, then the spec (with the actual caption recorded) is logged alongside results for reproducibility.

queries.query_text: Cedar apple rust
small yellow-orange spots on the upper leaf surface that enlarge and develop tiny black dots, with orange gelatinous tube-like structures forming on the underside of the leaf later in the season
apple tree leaves with bright orange-yellow spots and orange tubular growths underneath
An apple tree shows leaves with distinct orange or rust-colored blotches on top, and as the season progresses, small tube-like orange growths appear on the underside of the same spots.
how to manage an apple tree fungal disease that causes orange rust-colored leaf spots and requires a juniper or cedar host to complete its life cycle
Apple scab
olive-green to black velvety spots on leaves and fruit; leaves may pucker, curl, or drop prematurely; scabby, corky lesions develop on the fruit surface
apple tree with dark olive-green spots on leaves and scabby lesions on the fruit
An apple tree has velvety dark green to black spots scattered across its leaves, and the fruit shows rough, corky, dark patches on the skin.
how to control a fungal apple disease that causes dark scabby lesions on leaves and fruit, worse in wet spring weather
Black rot
purple-bordered leaf spots that enlarge into brown or tan lesions in a frogeye pattern, and fruit develops firm brown to black rotten areas often with concentric rings, eventually mummifying
apple tree with frogeye-pattern leaf spots and fruit turning black and shriveled
An apple tree shows circular brown leaf spots with purple margins, and some fruit on the tree has turned black, shrunken, and mummified.
how to manage an apple fungal disease that causes frogeye leaf spots and black mummified fruit, often associated with cankers on dead wood
Powdery mildew
white to grayish powdery fungal growth coating the surface of leaves, shoots, and sometimes fruit; affected leaves may curl, distort, or become stunted
cherry tree leaves covered in a white powdery coating with some curling and distortion
A tree's leaves and young shoots are dusted with a white, flour-like powdery coating, and some leaves appear curled or stunted.
how to treat a fungal disease that coats leaves in a white powdery film and thrives in warm, dry conditions with high humidity
Septoria leaf spot

small circular spots with dark brown margins and tan or gray centers on lower leaves first, often with tiny black specks visible in the center of each spot; severe infection causes yellowing and leaf drop
tomato plant with small tan-centered, brown-bordered spots on the lower leaves
A tomato plant's lower leaves have numerous small circular spots with dark edges and pale centers, and the leaves are starting to yellow and fall off.
how to manage a fungal tomato disease that causes small brown-bordered spots with tan centers on lower leaves, spread by water splash
Early blight
dark brown to black spots with concentric rings forming a target-like or bullseye pattern, usually starting on older lower leaves, often surrounded by a yellow halo
potato plant with bullseye-patterned brown spots on the older lower leaves
A potato plant's older leaves show dark brown spots with a distinct target-like ring pattern, and yellowing tissue surrounds each spot.
how to control a fungal potato disease that causes concentric ring target spot lesions on lower leaves
Bacterial spot

small, angular, water-soaked spots on leaves that turn dark brown to purplish-black, often with a yellow halo; spots may fall out leaving a shot-hole appearance; on fruit, spots become sunken and cracked
peach tree with small dark angular leaf spots and a shot-hole appearance, and sunken cracked spots on the fruit
A fruit tree has small dark, angular spots on its leaves, some of which have fallen out leaving small holes, and the fruit has sunken, cracked blemishes.
how to manage a bacterial disease of peach and other stone fruit trees causing small angular leaf spots that fall out leaving shot-holes, and sunken cracked fruit lesions
Fire blight

shoots and blossoms suddenly wilt, blacken, and die as if scorched by fire; the tips of infected branches often curl into a distinctive shepherd's crook shape; cankers with amber-colored bacterial ooze may appear on branches
apple or pear tree with blackened, scorched-looking shoots that curl over at the tip like a shepherd's crook
Branch tips on a fruit tree appear scorched and blackened as if burned, curling downward into a hook shape, with the blight spreading rapidly along the branch.
how to manage a bacterial disease of apple and pear trees causing scorched blackened shoots that curl into a hook shape, spread by insects and rain during bloom
